findings.title: The weekday bar chart shows a value for only one bar

location.description: The Bottles by weekday chart in the right card of the middle row

findings.viewer_experience: One bar carries the number 148 and the other six carry nothing and have no value axis, so the viewer can see Saturday is highest but cannot read how much lower the other days are.

current.value: One bar is labelled with a value, six bars have no value and the chart has no value axis.

findings.target: A viewer can read the value of every bar, either from a labelled axis or from a number on each bar.
findings.fix_direction: Add a value axis or a number on every bar so the six unlabelled days can be read.
findings.source: Tufte, The Visual Display of Quantitative Information

closed_when.check: Look at the bar chart: every bar can be read as a number, not only the highest one.

findings.title: The October comparison lines under the headline figures are small and pale

location.description: The small line under each of the four headline figures in the top row, such as the figure for October

findings.viewer_experience: The comparison with last month is what makes each headline figure meaningful, yet it is set in the smallest, palest text on the screen and does not say whether the figure went up or down.

current.value: The comparison line is small pale grey text and gives the old figure only, with no sign of direction.

findings.target: The comparison reads at a glance as better or worse than last month.
findings.fix_direction: Make the comparison easier to read and show the direction of change.

closed_when.check: Look at the top row: each headline figure has a comparison that can be read without leaning in and shows the direction of change.
